about: The introit of the First Sunday of Advent, the Mass that opens the liturgical year. Its antiphon is Psalm 24:1–3 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 25 in Hebrew) and its verse is the fourth verse of the same psalm. The offertory of this Mass returns to the same three verses.

seg.tr: To You, O my God, I lift up my soul. In You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

a.g: let me not be put to shame

ex.w012: The psalmist asks that his trust in God not be disappointed. The Hebrew volitive form and Greek optative also support reading these words as a plea.

nt.w012: “Erubéscam” can express a plea, “let me not be put to shame,” or a future statement, “I shall not be put to shame.” The Latin ending itself is shared by both readings.

seg.tr: Make Your ways known to me, O Lord, and teach me Your paths.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

ex.w035: In the doxology the verb remains unspoken. Liturgical usage supplies the wish “glory be”.

seg.nr: After the doxology the Introit antiphon is repeated from Ad te levávi to the psalm verse — by the choir at a sung Mass, by the priest himself at a low Mass.
